title: Reverse Bits
description:
Reverse all 32 positions of the unsigned binary representation of n, including its leading zero bits, and return the resulting unsigned integer. Reversing only the significant digits would lose the required fixed-width placement.

Example 1:

Input: n = 1
Output: 2147483648
Explanation: The least significant bit moves to position 31.

Example 2:

Input: n = 0
Output: 0
Explanation: Reversing 32 zero bits still gives zero.

Example 3:

Input: n = 2147483648
Output: 1
Explanation: The top bit moves to the least significant position.

Constraints:

  • 0 <= n <= 4,294,967,295 (unsigned 32-bit).
  • The returned integer is also in the unsigned 32-bit range.
